title: Foundations
summary: What Genesys Cloud CX is, where an organization lives, and how a voice conversation is supposed to move.

lessons.title: What Genesys Cloud CX is
lessons.summary: Genesys Cloud CX is a subscription contact-center platform with four nested packages, not a single feature switch.
paras: The overview article names four packages. Genesys Cloud CX 1 is the voice package: inbound and outbound voice, secure IVR, callbacks, and voice campaigns. CX 2 adds the digital channels and the quality and compliance layer on top of CX 1. CX 3 adds workforce engagement management and voice transcription minutes. CX 4 adds Agent Copilot, Journey Management, and a published AI token allotment: 30 tokens for a named user and 39 for a concurrent user.

Each higher package includes the lower ones. A design that needs scheduling and transcription is a CX 3 conversation. A design that needs Agent Copilot is a CX 4 conversation. The December 2023 feature-matrix PDF is a historical summary and does not describe CX 4 the way the current overview does.

lessons.title: Core regions and satellite media
lessons.summary: An organization is born in one core AWS region. Satellite regions carry media. They do not host the org.
paras: When an organization is created, Genesys Cloud deploys it in a core region and sends users to that region’s login URL. US East (N. Virginia, us-east-1) uses https://login.mypurecloud.com. US West (Oregon, us-west-2) uses https://login.usw2.pure.cloud. The FedRAMP region (US East 2, Ohio, us-east-2) uses https://login.use2.us-gov-pure.cloud. The regions article is the full table. Do not invent a login host for a row you have not opened.

Satellite regions exist for Global Media Fabric. They add places for call and audio paths, including recording storage, so media does not have to hairpin to the core. A satellite region cannot be the AWS region where the organization itself is deployed. Some core regions offer Genesys Cloud Voice and some do not. Voice coverage, including which countries can buy numbers, is a separate article from the org-deployment list.

cites.title: AWS regions for Genesys Cloud Voice

lessons.title: SIP, RTP, and what the trunk is doing
lessons.summary: SIP sets the call up. RTP moves the audio. They are different protocols, and Genesys trunks speak both.
paras: RFC 3261 is the Session Initiation Protocol. An INVITE offers a session, responses such as 100, 180, and 200 move the dialog along, and ACK confirms the 200. The media description inside that signaling is not the audio itself. RFC 3550 is RTP, the stream of audio packets. RFC 3711 is SRTP, the encrypted form of that stream. RFC 4733 is how telephone events such as DTMF digits can ride in the RTP stream instead of in the audio band.

BYOC Cloud places a SIP trunk between the Genesys Cloud media tier in AWS and a carrier or PBX that has a public address. The audio is RTP across the internet, so latency and loss on that path are part of the design. Example addresses in this lab use the documentation ranges in RFC 5737, such as 192.0.2.10, and are not a customer capture.

figure.caption: Signaling and media take different paths.

cards.back: RFC 3261. Session setup, not the audio packets.
RFC 3550. The audio stream.
RFC 3711. Encrypted RTP.
RFC 4733 telephone events, when digits must not depend on in-band audio.

lessons.title: What ACD is before you name a queue
lessons.summary: ACD picks an agent for a waiting interaction. The queue is the waiting line. Skills, utilization, and On Queue decide who is eligible.
paras: Genesys Cloud queues are the waiting lines. An agent enters the queues they belong to by choosing On Queue. A queue name is unique, cannot contain special characters, and can hold at most 5,000 members. The queue also belongs to a division, which is how access control reaches it.

Routing methods decide how that waiting line offers work: standard, predictive, bullseye, preferred agent, and conditional group routing. Evaluation methods decide what “has the skills” means. Utilization decides whether an agent who is already busy may take another interaction. Those controls are the rest of this lab. This lesson only fixes the vocabulary.

lessons.title: Digital conversations beside voice
lessons.summary: Voice is one media. Architect also has inbound message, email, and chat flows, and queues track those medias separately.
paras: The Architect home page lists inbound message, inbound email, and inbound chat alongside inbound call. In-queue flows exist for calls, email, and messages. Call flows ship with a default in-queue flow that is not published until you publish it. Email and message queues do not get that built-in default. You create those in-queue flows yourself.

Utilization counts medias separately. The documented defaults are one voice call, one email, one callback, up to four chats, up to four messages, and up to four workitems. A designer who copies a voice queue and expects the same in-queue music on email has skipped the flow-type list.

lessons.title: Divisions, before roles get complicated
lessons.summary: A division groups objects inside one organization. It is not a second org, and the Home division cannot be deleted.
paras: Administrators group configuration objects into divisions and then grant roles against those divisions. A queue lives in one division. Users reach objects by holding a role in the division that contains them. Every organization has a Home division. You can move objects into and out of Home. You cannot delete Home.

Until you create more divisions, new configuration objects land in a way the article describes through the All division concept: All grants organization-wide access, and transactional objects such as conversations, recordings, presence history, and audit data pick up division associations as they move. You move an object between divisions. You do not add a second division membership to the same queue.

lessons.title: How to read a Genesys page without inventing the rest
lessons.summary: This lab cites the Resource Center, the Developer Center, Genesys Education, and RFCs. The page wins when they differ.
paras: Implementation facts in this lab were checked against public pages on 14 October 2026. Certifications are the names on the Genesys Education cloud exam catalog, including GC-GCP and GC-GCD in the catalog header. Specialist rows are named there without this lab inventing extra exam codes. Community threads still say GCX- in places. Treat the catalog as the current list.

The Developer Center’s client-credentials guide is the source for the token request, not a blog. The Resource Center is the source for admin behavior. When a summary on a help page and a sentence lower on the same page disagree, read the procedure, not only the generated summary. Fair-use numbers change. This lab points at the policy instead of copying the rate card.

lessons.title: Prerequisites before the first trunk
lessons.summary: BYOC Cloud needs a public carrier address, an open port plan, and a real location. The org subscription has to include the telephony product you intend to use.
paras: The BYOC Cloud quick start assumes the organization exists and the BYOC Cloud product is on the subscription. You then work the carrier requirements, add a physical location, create a BYOC Carrier or BYOC PBX trunk, attach that trunk to an outbound route, and add number plans as needed. The location is not cosmetic. Emergency calling with BYOC uses it, and Genesys warns that it is not responsible for emergency calls that ride a BYOC trunk.

New BYOC Cloud trunks should use the Dynamic Cloud Voice platform. RTP still crosses the internet, so you judge latency before you promise a voice quality number you have not measured. Monitoring cloud media resources is the documented place to look at that cloud media, not a packet capture from a laptop as the only tool.
